faqs.question: What does Single Antigen Bead Assay measure?
faqs.answer: Single Antigen Bead Assay measures specific proteins called Class I & Class II human leukocyte antigens (HLAs) on the surface of cells.

faqs.question: Why is Single Antigen Bead Assay done?
faqs.answer: • To assess compatibility between organ donors and recipients prior to transplantation • To identify any potential immune reactions that may occur after transplantation • To guide the selection of suitable donors for individuals requiring organ transplants involving the immune system

faqs.question: When is Single Antigen Bead Assay recommended and who should take the test?
faqs.answer: The Single Antigen Bead Assay is recommended in the following scenarios: • Prior to organ transplantation to determine compatibility between donors and recipients • For individuals requiring transplants involving the immune system, such as bone marrow or kidney transplants

faqs.question: What if the results of the Single Antigen Bead Assay are abnormal?
faqs.answer: Abnormal results of the Single Antigen Bead Assay may indicate a higher risk of rejection or immune complications after organ transplantation.

faqs.question: What to expect during the Single Antigen Bead Assay?
faqs.answer: A small blood sample will be collected from your arm. The sample will be sent to a laboratory where it will be analysed using a bead-based immunoassay.

faqs.question: What preparations are required before the Single Antigen Bead Assay?
faqs.answer: • Provide a complete clinical history and information about the relationship between the recipient and donor. • Ensure that you have the necessary consent forms and any requested photographs ready for submission. • Inform your doctor if you have any specific requirements.

faqs.question: What other tests may be ordered with Single Antigen Bead Assay?
faqs.answer: • HLA tissue typing: This test determines human leukocyte antigen (HLA) compatibility between donors and recipients for organ transplantation. • Crossmatch tests: These tests assess compatibility between donor and recipient by checking for pre-existing antibodies in the recipient's blood. • Transplant biopsy: If abnormalities are detected, a biopsy may be performed to further evaluate the transplanted organ.

faqs.question: What is the Single Antigen Bead Assay also known as?
faqs.answer: HLA antibody testing, Donor compatibility testing, or HLA typing

faqs.question: What is organ transplantation?
faqs.answer: Organ transplantation is a medical procedure in which a diseased or damaged organ is replaced with a healthy organ from a donor. This may be necessary due to organ failure or life-threatening conditions. Transplants can involve organs such as the kidney, liver, heart, lung, pancreas, or bone marrow.
